why: The tests step for porting scripts/typecheck.sh to scripts/typecheck.ts (docs/plan/quests/port-typecheck-PLAN.md), in today's tooling. New laws: N1 (the program's commands, lines, exit code and lock on the test layers, 100 runs), N2 (judge over generated looks, 200 runs), N3 (LocksFile.layer on a disk in memory, a walk of takes, releases, cancels, kills, ended commands, reused pids and an old 1419 script's overwrite, 100 runs), N4 (Mercurial's break race, in two fixed orders), N5 (CommandsProcess on real node children, in scripts/typecheck.integration.test.ts) and N6 (ProcessesPs on saved pgrep and ps output). Four test layers and a test helper in scripts/typecheck/. E1's body changed as the plan says. E2 to E6 and I1 to I6 now start the script with node; E2, E3, E4 and E6 also changed where the plan said invocation only: a fixed 250 ms or 100 ms pause passed with no lock at all once the wrapper became node (about 600 ms to its first command, measured here), so those laws now wait until the second wrapper prints 1419's waiting line or its compiler starts. Every new law is red now because the product files do not exist; every older caps law not about the typecheck stays green. Each law was first seen green, and each plant red, on a throwaway reference implementation of the plan written in the scratch folder and removed before the commit; the plants must run again on the build's code at review.

note: Plants ran once each on the reference implementation, by copy and restore, and are not committed. N3 does not catch the two break-race plants (its walk never lands two breakers between a read and a removal); N4 catches both, which is the plan's split. The reference implementation's first wait sat inside an uninterruptible acquire and hung on interrupt, so N3 gained a cancel move. With the wait for the waiting line, E6's cancel reaches a waiter inside NodeRuntime.runMain, which exits with a code, not by the signal, unless the program re-raises the signal after its finalizers; the reference implementation did that and E6 passed. caches.ts now reads scripts/typecheck.ts, as the plan's C0 row says, so the build must keep the check command's --tsBuildInfoFile items in that file, or an amendment moves the read. Tests ran in this Linux box with CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true; the 0178 guard refused none. pnpm lint fails in two parts only because the product is missing: skillscheck.sh (the three SKILL.md files the build edits) and workflow-lint.ts (scripts/typecheck.ts does not exist). The list ratchet passes. No pnpm typecheck ran; the new files join .agents/tsconfig.json in the build. A narrow tsc over the new test files and the reference implementation found no error in the test files. 1419's I5 and then I4 each flaked once here (the stand-in compiler never started): Linux names the stand-in after its link, Node renames its main thread, and named.mjs writes the name back, so a pgrep could see the name and the next one miss it. The stand-in now writes a ready file after it sets its name, and the helper waits for that first; five runs in a row passed after.
